Fishbowl keeps the records: Fishbowl and your books stay in charge of customers, inventory levels, lot tracking and invoicing. We store each restaurant's order guide with your prices, which you edit whenever they change, plus every order its chef places through the app.

Fishbowl's app is for your warehouse: Fishbowl Advanced Mobile turns a phone into a barcode scanner for your staff: picking, receiving and counts. Ours belongs to the chef and does one thing: ordering. Your warehouse keeps scanning in Fishbowl's app.

QuickBooks still gets its invoices from Fishbowl: Shipping an order in Fishbowl still creates its invoice in QuickBooks, exactly as it does today. We stop at the point your desk has the order, so your books and your accountant see no change.

@graph.name: How restaurants get started on the app
@graph.description: Fishbowl stays exactly as it is. You send us a spreadsheet, and we set up the restaurants.

step.name: Send us one Fishbowl export
step.text: A spreadsheet out of Fishbowl is usually all we need: what each restaurant buys and what it pays, item by item.

step.name: We open each restaurant's account
step.text: We load the guide, the account opens, and the chef downloads the app. Most kitchens place a first order the same day.

step.name: The first orders your desk did not take by phone
step.text: Each one was read over by the chef, carries an order number and its send time, and lands where you asked for it.

@graph.name: Should we look for a Fishbowl Inventory alternative to get spoken restaurant orders?

acceptedAnswer.text: No. Fishbowl goes on running your counts, lot tracking, picking and QuickBooks invoicing. What we add is for the restaurant that phones you: its chef talks each item into our app, looks it over and hits send, so nobody at your desk takes it down during a call.

@graph.name: Is VoiceOrder Solutions better than Fishbowl Inventory?

acceptedAnswer.text: They do different jobs, and VoiceOrder Solutions is no Fishbowl Inventory replacement. Fishbowl handles the order from the moment it is entered: counts, picking, lots and your books. Our one job comes earlier: a chef voices the order in an app and checks it first, rather than phoning your desk.

@graph.name: Doesn't Fishbowl already offer a B2B portal?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes. Fishbowl lists its own portal among its plan add-ons, and partner portals and sales-rep apps feed their orders into Fishbowl as sales orders. That suits a chef happy to log in and pick each item from a list or a search. Our app is for the chef who prefers to say it aloud, then read the list over before sending.

@graph.name: Our retail chains send EDI. Can restaurant orders arrive the same way?

acceptedAnswer.text: We can send each restaurant order over EDI, yes. Fishbowl's EDI is set up for retailer trading partners, through the EDI services it works with. Whether your Fishbowl EDI setup will accept orders from us is something we work out with you in the demo. If it cannot, email, or our API if your setup takes it, will carry the order instead.

@graph.name: Does Fishbowl connect to VoiceOrder Solutions, or will my desk still type orders?

acceptedAnswer.text: They do not connect: the two are sold and supported apart, and each vendor stands behind its own software only. Through EDI or our API, Fishbowl may accept the order with no retyping, if your setup allows; the demo is where that gets checked. By email, someone at your desk enters it from the attached file, which the chef went over before sending, rather than from a call. A call placed the old way still gets no number from us. Fishbowl offers an API, so other order tools can connect to it too, and its AI assistant, in beta, drafts purchase orders, transfers and sales orders for your staff to approve.

@graph.name: We run Fishbowl beside QuickBooks. Can you deliver orders into QuickBooks?

acceptedAnswer.text: QuickBooks is one of our delivery formats. With Fishbowl, though, your sales orders start in Fishbowl. Fishbowl's own QuickBooks page says sales orders do not transfer automatically between the two, and that invoices flow from Fishbowl to QuickBooks, so do not count on an order we put into QuickBooks reaching Fishbowl. A file, EDI or the API is the more direct choice, and the demo settles which.

@graph.name: How fast is setup, and what does it cost?

acceptedAnswer.text: Setup takes 24 to 48 hours for most distributors, and nothing in Fishbowl changes. Fishbowl publishes starting prices for its plans; we give each distributor a quote and publish no figure. Any Fishbowl Inventory alternative means a new stock system, a data move and retraining the warehouse. Shifting some restaurant calls into an app asks for none of that.
